html:
The Kingdom of the Two Sicilies joined the kingdoms of Naples and Sicily into one state, the largest in Italy before unification, from 1816 to 1861. The map uses the name already in 1783, 1800 and 1815, when the two were still separate kingdoms under one Bourbon king.

A Spanish Bourbon prince, Charles, took both kingdoms in 1734 and 1735. His son Ferdinand ruled them for over sixty years. In 1799 Neapolitan liberals set up the short-lived Parthenopean Republic, crushed within months. Napoleon took Naples in 1806 and gave it to his brother and then to Joachim Murat, while Ferdinand held Sicily under British protection.

Back in Naples, Ferdinand merged the two crowns in 1816. The kingdom built Italy's first railway, from Naples to Portici, in 1839, but its rule was harsh. The rising in Palermo in January 1848 was one of the first of the revolutions of 1848. In 1860 Garibaldi landed in Sicily with his Thousand volunteers and took the kingdom, which joined Italy in 1861.
